scope.description: Five trials that each commit a value, partition and stall the leader, let a successor commit a different value, then compare the FSM values of the stalled leader and the successor after the leader's VerifyLeader returned, recording the verify endpoint, the two values, both terms and the stall counters.
assumptions: The mock FSM records each applied command in order, so its last value is what the node's state machine holds for that key; the harness reads it through the package's own test helper rather than by reaching into raft state.
The value committed before the partition has reached every node, checked by waiting after the apply, so the two nodes start from the same state.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, a 900ms store stall that blocks the leader's main loop, and in-memory transports in one process.
excluded: A networked deployment, and any read path other than the FSM value the mock records.

basis.prefix: Each trial builds four real Raft instances of the same shape as the earlier witness probe: three voters bootstrapped as Voter and one non-voter joined through the leader's AddNonvoter call, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, and only the elected leader's log store armed with a 900ms stall. It emits assurance_stale_read_setup, commits the value 'old' through the leader and waits for it to appear on all nodes, disconnects the leader from both other voters and from the non-voter, registers VerifyLeader, waits 30ms, arms the stall, drives one Apply to block the leader's main loop, waits up to two seconds for another voter to report Leader and has that successor apply the value 'new', reconnects only the non-voter after the configured delay, waits for the verify future, then emits assurance_stale_read_result with the endpoint, the stalled leader's last FSM value, the successor's last FSM value, whether those differ, both terms, the stalled leader's state and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyRegisteredThenStalled.

comparisons.description: Conditional on the verify reporting success: whether the stalled leader's FSM value differed from the successor's, which is the stale read a caller would have taken.
The stalled leader's own FSM never advanced past the value committed before the partition.
The successor committed the different value, so the cluster did move on while the old leader was stalled.

before.description: Six trials that each build a three-voter plus one-non-voter cluster, register a VerifyLeader request at the leader while it is isolated from every peer, stall its main loop inside StoreLogs for 900ms, then reconnect only the non-voter after 250 to 500ms and record the verify endpoint, when a different server was first sampled in Leader state, whether that preceded the verdict, the terms involved and the stall counters.
assumptions: The stalling log store models a leader whose disk stall blocks its own main loop; it is a supplied dependency, not a change to production logic.
Reconnecting the non-voter is a legal topology change: the transport is simply reconnected to a server that remains in the leader's latest configuration as a non-voter.

HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and a 900ms stall mean the leader's lease case cannot run during the stall while a voter majority can campaign at 200ms and elect a successor.
In-memory transports in one process, so RPC round trips are far faster than in a networked cluster.
excluded: Multi-host clocks and process-level suspensions; and any case where the leader's own term is raised, since the partition keeps it at its old term.

prefix.before: Each trial builds four real Raft instances in one process with their own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts; the three voters get a log store whose StoreLogs sleeps 900ms while armed, and only the elected leader's store is armed. The three voters are bootstrapped as Voter and the fourth node joins through the leader's AddNonvoter call. The trial emits assurance_registered_setup, disconnects the leader from both other voters and from the non-voter, calls VerifyLeader on the leader, waits 30ms so the main loop registers the request, arms the stall and drives one Apply so the leader's main loop blocks inside StoreLogs, starts a 1ms sampler over all four servers, then after the configured delay reconnects only the leader and the non-voter and waits for the verify future. It emits assurance_registered_result with the endpoint, the verdict time, whether another server was sampled in Leader state and when, the maximum term seen, the leader's term and state, and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyRegisteredThenStalled.

before.description: The stalled leader returned VerifyLeader success even though it could reach no voter for the whole window.
A successor was sampled in Leader state before the verify returned, so the verdict and the successor overlapped.
Conditional on a successor preceding the verdict: whether the leader still reported success. Holds means the stale-read verdict was witnessed.

revision_reason: The earlier revision showed the overlap between a successful VerifyLeader and a concurrent successor but never read the stalled leader's FSM, which the account recorded as a limitation. This revision keeps the same build, partition, stall and reconnection and adds committed values: a value applied and replicated before the partition, a different value applied by the successor afterwards, and reads of the mock FSM on both nodes after the verify returns. Event names are new because the fields differ; the setup and result structure is unchanged.
